MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle: IT CYBERSECURITY SPECIALIST (INFOSEC) (ADVANCED CYBERSECURITY ZERO TRUST SPECIALIST)
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: The experience described in your resume will be evaluated and screened from the Office of Personnel Management's (OPMs) basic qualifications requirements. See: Competency-Based Qualification Standard for the Information Technology Management Series, 2210 for OPM qualification standards, competencies and specialized experience needed to perform the duties of the position as described in the MAJOR DUTIES and QUALIFICATIONS sections of this announcement by 12/09/2026 Applicant must have directly applicable experience that demonstrates the possession of the knowledge, skills, abilities and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Qualifying experience may have been acquired in any public or private sector job, but will clearly demonstrate past experience in the application of the particular competencies/knowledge, skills and abilities necessary to successfully perform the duties of the position. You must have specialized experience sufficient to demonstrate that you have acquired all the competencies necessary to perform at a level equivalent in difficulty, responsibility, and complexity to the next lower grade (GS/GG-13) in the Federal service and are prepared to take on greater responsibility. Generally, this would include one year or more of such specialized experience. Specialized experience for this position includes: Architecting or engineering enterprise Zero Trust security architectures across multiple pillars (e.g., User/Identity, Credential, and Access Management (ICAM), Device, Network, Application, Data, Visibility, Automation) for on-premises networks, classified enclaves, or cross-domain solutions. Providing consultative systems security engineering guidance and architectural alignment reviews to program-level teams deploying solutions into hybrid multi-cloud environments. Evaluating and resolving complex systems security engineering flaws, multi-domain integration challenges, and emerging technology security designs (such as Super Intelligence (SI)/Machine Learning (ML) platforms and containerized pipelines). Authoring technical engineering directives, reference baselines, and architectural white papers to advise, brief, and defend strategic cybersecurity strategies before executive leadership and inter-agency stakeholders. Specifically you will be evaluated on the following competencies: Enterprise Architecture - Knowledge of principles, concepts, and methods of enterprise architecture to align information technology (IT) strategy, plans, and systems with the mission, goals, structure, and processes of the organization. Decision Making - Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change. Leadership - Influences, motivates, and challenges others; adapts leadership styles to a variety of situations. Accountability - Holds self and others accountable for measurable high-quality, timely, and cost-effective results. Determines objectives, sets priorities, and delegates work. Accepts responsibility for mistakes. Complies with established control systems and rules. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Note: Clients and customers include any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government. In addition to meeting qualifications, your application package must reflect the applicable experience to meet the Individual Occupational Requirements for the 2210, series as listed below: Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations.

Details.JobSummary: Join the Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency (DCSA) Office of the Chief Information Security Officer as a Senior Cybersecurity Zero Trust Engineer. You will serve as the technical authority architecting/engineering Zero Trust solutions across on-premises, classified enclaves, AI platforms, and cross-domain systems, while providing consultative guidance to cloud programs. Make a direct impact safeguarding the integrity of our nation's trusted workforce and technologies.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Our Mission Through vetting, industry engagement, education, and counterintelligence and insider threat support, secure the trustworthiness of the United States Government's workforce, the integrity of its cleared contractor support, and the uncompromised nature of its technologies, services, and supply chains. Our Vision DCSA's elite security experts illuminate national security risks to empower faster, smarter decision-making that protects American innovation and resilience to enable mission success. DCSA Strategic Execution Plan The Defense Counterintelligence and Security Agency stands at the intersection of government-wide trusted workforce, national security, and industrial base protection. Guided by the Secretary of War's National Defense Strategy, Deputy Secretary's Warfighting Acquisition Transformation efforts, and Trusted Workforce 2.0, our mission is to deliver data-driven, threat-informed, and customer-trusted security services at scale. The FY2026 - 2028 DCSA Strategic Execution Plan defines six strategic priorities for the agency: Deliver NBIS Deploy NI2 to Modernize Industrial Security Modernize and Sustain Trusted Workforce Determinations Rebuild the Workforce Compact Operate as a Customer-Centric Business Drive Audit-Ready Integration and Agency Efficiency with AI
MajorDuties: As a IT CYBERSECURITY SPECIALIST (INFOSEC) (ADVANCED CYBERSECURITY ZERO TRUST SPECIALIST) you will be responsible for the following duties: Authors and establishes enterprise Zero Trust reference architectures, target states, and systems security engineering standards across agency on-premises data centers, classified enclaves, and cross-domain solutions. Provides senior consultative cybersecurity architecture/engineering guidance and alignment reviews to program-level engineering teams deploying solutions across hybrid multi-cloud environments. Engineers robust security architectures across the seven DoW Zero Trust pillars to protect critical enterprise background investigation systems, personnel vetting platforms, and artificial intelligence environments. Formulates, issues, and interprets agency-level cybersecurity engineering directives, policies, and architectural mandates governing major IT capital investments and modern software acquisitions. Authors and establishes enterprise Zero Trust reference architectures, target states, and systems security engineering standards across agency on-premises data centers, classified enclaves, and cross-domain solutions. The Office Under Secretary of Defense for Intelligence and Security established a Targeted Local Market Supplement (TLMS) for certain Science, Technology, Engineering, Mathematics, and Cyber positions within the Defense Civilian Intelligence Personnel System. Eligibility for the TLMS is based on cyber work roles within certain occupational series and on the work performed. This vacancy is designated as a STEM and/or Cyber position and pay for the incumbent will be based on the STEM and Cyber Pay Table

MajorDuties: This position serves as Senior technical advisor to the Supervisory IT Specialist and Division leadership in providing authoritative recommendations on engineering priorities, architectural decisions, and long-term technology roadmaps. Other duties may include: Performs as the senior technical authority for the design, implementation, and lifecycle management of enterprise desktop capabilities, cloud administration of systems/software management, security baselines, client operating system configurations, and endpoint software/hardware standards. Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: Resolving complex architectural, transport and routing challenges across native, afloat, cloud and hybrid enterprise environments. 2. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: Serving as a senior technical advisor, representing the command in cross-functional, joint and inter-agency working groups. 3. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: Briefing Flag/General Officers, Senior Executive Service, and civilian executives. 4. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Details.JobSummary: You will serve as an IT SPECIALIST(NETWORK) in the C2 & NETWORKS DIVISION of NAVWARSYSCEN PACIFIC SAN DIEGO CA. Temporary actions taken under this announcement may be made permanent without further competition. Temporary actions taken under this announcement may be terminated at any time before the established not-to-exceed date. Temporary promotions may be extended up to 5 years at the discretion of management and in accordance with applicable regulations.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will serve as a technical authority for the planning, systems engineering, testing, and implementation of Naval enterprise network modernization initiatives, ensuring adherence to DoD Zero Trust frameworks.
You will resolve complex architectural, transport, and routing challenges across native, afloat, cloud, and hybrid enterprise environments and globally distributed WAN/BAN/LAN infrastructures.
You will provide daily technical oversight and coordination for Naval enterprise operations supporting CTF 1010, Task Group 1010.10, and Tenth Fleet operational orders.
You will direct dynamic network maneuvers, troubleshooting, and defensive security policy enforcement during live operations to maintain operational continuity and mission assurance.
You will translate operational network findings and performance metrics into validated engineering data to inform acquisition programs, PEOs, and SYSCOM roadmaps.
You will serve as a senior technical advisor to CTF 1010 and Tenth Fleet leadership, representing the command in cross-functional, joint, and inter-agency working groups.

You will brief Flag/General Officers (O-6 and above), Senior Executive Service (SES), and civilian executives, translating complex network telemetry and cyber vulnerabilities into actionable strategic decisions.

You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. 1) Applicants must have IT-related experience demonstrating each of the competencies listed below (required for all grade levels): Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Decision Making- Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change. Information Management- Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems. Interpersonal Skills- Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Hold a current Cisco Certified Network Professional CCNP) certification; B. Administering Cisco FirePower appliances and Firepower Management Center (FMC). This includes configuring or maintaining firewall policies, access controls, upgrades or troubleshooting; C. Configuring, maintaining, and troubleshooting Cisco routers and switches. This includes Transmission Control Protocol/Internet Protocol (TCP/IP), routing such as Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) or Border Gateway Protocol (BGP), diagnostic commands, circuit or connectivity troubleshooting, configuration backups, and tested maintenance or upgrades. D. Independently developing or modifying enterprise Local Area Network (LAN) or Wide Area Network (WAN) designs and coordinating implementation requirements. Relevant work includes routing, capacity, redundancy, segmentation, WAN transport, or cloud connectivity; documenting designs; and coordinating requirements, testing, or changes with application teams, vendors, or other technical groups. E. Analyzing network performance and vulnerability findings and implementing or coordinating corrective changes. Relevant work includes analyzing and working with logs, network telemetry, dashboards, alerts, performance baselines, Nessus or comparable vulnerability tools, firewall or access controls, segmentation, and verification of remediation or restored service.

Details.JobSummary: Consistently ranked as among the best places to work in the Department of the Interior (DOI), and the top 10% of all agency subcomponents, the Office of Inspector General is an independent and objective unit within DOI working to promote economy, efficiency, and effectiveness and to prevent and detect waste, fraud and abuse within the DOI. We offer exceptional work-life benefits, including flexible work schedules, ample training opportunities, and a comprehensive employee recognition program.
Details.SubAgencyName: Information Technology Division, Office of Management
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Office of Inspector General (OIG) mission is to promote economy and efficiency, and prevent and detect waste, fraud, abuse and mismanagement in the programs and operations for the Department of the Interior (DOI). The OIG conducts fair, objective and neutral audits, inspections, evaluations, investigations and reviews. Through our oversight work, we help to safeguard taxpayer dollars from fraud and mismanagement identifying ways to improve DOI's programs and operations. Our values of integrity, objectivity, impact and excellence guide employee behavior and decisions at all levels. This position is located in Herndon, VA and is conveniently located near shops, restaurants, public transportation, and offers free parking.
MajorDuties: This position is with the Office of Inspector General, Information Technology Division, in Herndon, Virginia. This office is responsible for IT systems administration, telecommunications, and network management services. As a Information Technology Specialist (Network Services) you will be responsible for serving as a primary Cisco network administrator and enterprise Wide Area Network (WAN) architect. Major duties include: Designs and maintains multi-site connectivity, routing, capacity, redundancy, segmentation, and secure connections to cloud or shared services. Configures, maintains, upgrades, and troubleshoots Cisco routers, switches, network services, and circuits. Resolves complex faults, tests changes, maintains configuration records and backups, and verifies operational recovery. Administers Cisco FirePower and FMC protections; applies segmentation, least privilege, and Zero Trust networking principles. Coordinates network dependencies with directory and identity services and cybersecurity officials. Conducts or coordinates network vulnerability testing, analyzes findings, reports risks, and leads remediation within assigned authority. Analyzes router, firewall, circuit, SD-WAN, and cloud telemetry. Develops dashboards, alerts, baselines, and proactive monitoring or AIOps approaches to detect degradation, tune performance, and improve reliability. Leads network integrations, migrations, and implementations with agency officials, application owners, technical specialists, and service providers. Plans dependencies, testing, transition and recovery; documents architecture and briefs leadership on alternatives, risks, and results.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: All qualification and time-in-grade (if applicable) requirements must be met within 30 days of the closing date of this announcement. You must meet the minimum qualification requirements as stated in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Operating Manual, Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, http://www.opm.gov/qualifications/Standards/group-stds/gs-prof.asp. Basic Requirement: Applicants must have IT-related experience demonstrating the following competencies appropriate to, or above, the level of this position. For vacancies below the full-performance level of the position, the basic requirement will be evaluated on a developmental basis. Your resume and work experience should clearly support your ability to meet these competencies and will be evaluated as part of the entire application process. Attention to Detail- experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been asked by others to review their work or data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards. Customer Service- experience maintaining relationships with customers, assessing current information technology needs of customers, and developing or identifying information technology products and services that are tailored to meet customer needs. Oral Communication- briefing mid-level management and IT staff on the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the communication of technical information to a non-technical audience. Problem Solving- identifying alternatives to address complex information technology-related issues by gathering and applying information from a variety of sources that provide a number of potential solutions. In addition to meeting the basic requirement, you must have one year specialized experience. One year of specialized experience at the next lower broadband NH-03, equivalent to the GS-13 grade level or equivalent in other pay systems. Specialized experience is described as: Experience managing, configuring, sustaining, and optimizing enterprise data platforms and integrated data environments, including cloud-based and hybrid data ecosystems, to support large-scale data ingestion, storage, governance, integration, visualization, and decision-support capabilities across multiple functional and operational domains. Experience monitoring, testing, troubleshooting, and validating data integrations and interoperability solutions between enterprise systems, mission applications, authoritative data sources, external partner organizations, and analytics platforms; resolving data quality issues, failed data exchanges, reporting discrepancies, access control problems, and system integration challenges to ensure reliable and trusted data availability. Experience leading technical planning and execution of enterprise data modernization initiatives, including data migration efforts, platform enhancements, user acceptance testing, pilot implementations, phased deployment strategies, production transitions, sustainment planning, and stakeholder engagement activities to translate mission and business requirements into data architecture, integration, and operational solutions. Experience in supporting acquisition, governance, and lifecycle management activities for enterprise data and analytics capabilities, including conducting market research, developing technical requirements, evaluating proposed solutions, assessing performance, and analyzing cost, schedule, scope, licensing, cybersecurity, and sustainment impacts associated with enterprise data technologies and services. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: This position is under the DoW Acquisition Workforce Personnel Demonstration Project (AcqDemo) within Title 5 Competitive Service. For more information on Acq Demo please go to the DoW AcqDemo website at https://acqdemo.hci.mil/ and Fact Sheet at https://acqdemo.hci.mil/faq.html Purpose of Position: To provide technical oversight, coordination, and operational support for enterprise data integration initiatives.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Join WarU and be a part of a world-class Department of War organization committed to training and supporting Warfighting acquisition professionals. In addition to training courses, WarU offers a variety of learning events and experiences, provides tools and resources to help on the job, conducts direct assistance to organizations, and offers access to an entire community of practitioners, experts and policy makers. WarU promotes a culture of lifelong learning both for faculty and staff and for the members of the Warfighting Acquisition Workforce they serve. Join our dynamic team and help give our military the competitive advantage they need.
MajorDuties: The Data Integration Management and Support Specialist serves as a senior Information Technology professional responsible for providing technical oversight, operational support, and coordination of enterprise data integration activities. The incumbent supports system interoperability, data governance, modernization initiatives, and contractor performance while ensuring compliance with federal information technology standards. The position also provides technical guidance to management, program offices, and stakeholders to ensure effective implementation, performance, and sustainment of enterprise data systems. Duties include: Provides senior-level technical oversight of enterprise data integration operations involving learning management systems, workforce systems, identity management platforms, reporting applications, and external data sources. Oversees the planning, implementation, monitoring, and sustainment of data integration solutions to ensure operational continuity, system compatibility, and reliable information exchange. Evaluates integration requirements, operational performance, technical documentation, and system dependencies to identify deficiencies and recommend corrective actions. Evaluates data management practices and recommends improvements to ensure the accuracy, integrity, consistency, accessibility, and reliability of enterprise information. Serves as a senior technical advisor on system interoperability, enterprise architecture, cloud-based technologies, automation capabilities, and data modernization initiatives. Develops and reviews technical requirements, statements of work, performance standards, and evaluation criteria for proposed technology solutions and contractor services. Provides technical recommendations concerning contractor performance, acquisition risks, cost considerations, implementation schedules, and sustainment requirements. Supports Contracting Officer's Representative (COR) functions, as assigned and consistent with applicable appointment requirements and contracting regulations. Other Work Requirements and/or Conditions of Employment: Requires knowledge of: the substantive nature of agency programs and activities; agency missions, policies, and objectives; management principles and processes; and the analytical and evaluative methods and techniques for assessing program development or execution and improving organizational effectiveness and efficiency. Requires an understanding of basic budgetary and financial management principles and techniques as they relate to long range planning of programs and objectives. Requires skill in the application of fact finding and investigative techniques; oral and written communications; and development of presentations and reports. Analyzes and evaluates (on a quantitative or qualitative basis) the effectiveness of program operations in meeting established goals and objectives. Develops life cycle cost analyses of projects or performing cost benefit or economic evaluations of current or projected programs. Advises on the potential benefits/uses of automation to improve the efficiency of administrative support or program operations. Evaluates and advises on the organization, methods, and procedures for providing administrative support systems such as records, communications, directives, forms, files, and documentation. Stays abreast of changes and trends in primary functional area, continuously researching, gaining and sharing knowledge in federal communities of practice. Maintains digital and data analysis fluency. Maintains currency and actively uses university technology, digital and social media platforms. Focuses on the needs of the customer in a modern acquisition and learning environment that is subject to continual change with respect to platforms, networks and delivery. Serves as a thinking partner with stakeholders and customers, continuously improving product and service delivery to provide the right knowledge and service at the point of need through synchronous and asynchronous methods. Builds relationships and collaborates with peers and program management leaders from all organizations within the area of responsibility. Elicits feedback to shape the policies, processes and procedures that produce a frictionless experience for the customers and stakeholders.

ACTIVE DUTY SERVICE MEMBERS: The Veterans Opportunity to Work (VOW) Act requires federal agencies to treat an eligible active duty service member as a veteran, disabled veteran, and preference eligible (as applicable) when applying for civil service positions before the effective release or discharge date. Appointment of military members before the release or discharge date is permissible if the member is on terminal leave. At the time the active duty member applies for a civil position, he or she must submit a "certification" memo in lieu of a DD-Form 214, Certificate of Release or Discharge from Active Duty. Active duty members applying for a civil service position without submitting a valid certification memo or DD-Form 214 with their application will render the member ineligible for the position. The certification memo must originate from the member's military service branch on official letterhead and contain the following: Name/Rank/Grade of Service Member Branch of Armed Forces Dates of Active Service (Start and End Date(s) Expected Date of Discharge/Release from Active Duty Terminal leave start date (if applicable) Expected character of service/discharge and type of separation (i.e. separation or retirement) Must be certified within 120 days of anticipated discharge Signature by, or by direction of the adjutant, personnel office, unit commander, or higher headquarters commander. Note: The VOW Act provides tentative preference. If appointed, a DD Form-214 must be submitted upon receipt. Note: It is the applicant's responsibility to verify that information and documents entered or uploaded are received, legible, and accurate.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.PositionTitle: Deputy Director and Chief Technology Officer
MatchedObjectDescriptor.DepartmentName: Department of Health and Human Services
MatchedObjectDescriptor.SubAgency: Office of Health Technology and Products
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution. Candidates will not be hired based on their race, sex, color, religion, or national origin. To meet the minimum qualification requirements for this position, you must show that you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) and Technical Qualifications (TQ) related to this position within your resume - NOT TO EXCEED 2 PAGES. Resumes over the 2-page limit, will not be reviewed beyond page 2 or may be disqualified. Your resume should include examples of experience, education, and accomplishments applicable to the qualification(s). If your resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of these qualifications, you may not receive consideration for the position. There is NO requirement to prepare a narrative statement specifically addressing the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQs) or the Technical Qualifications (TQs). TECHNICAL QUALIFICATIONS (TQs): Your resume should demonstrate accomplishments that would satisfy the technical qualifications. TQ 1: Demonstrated executive-level knowledge and experience with the relevant laws and policies of the nation's health care programs, including interoperability and administrative transaction standards to reduce burden and support modern data exchange approaches, including trends in the nation's digital health technology ecosystem for payment and delivery system innovations and reform. TQ 2: Demonstrated executive-level experience leading enterprise IT engineering, technical architecture, shared platform and product strategy including full product lifecycle (discovery, design, development, launch, operations, iteration, and retirement) and the adoption of artificial intelligence and advanced automation that serves beneficiaries, providers, plans and states. EXECUTIVE CORE QUALIFICATIONS (ECQs): In addition to the Technical Qualification Requirements listed above, all new entrants into the Senior Executive Service (SES) under a career appointment will be assessed for executive competency against the following five mandatory ECQs. If your 2-page resume does not reflect demonstrated evidence of the ECQs and TQs, you may not receive further consideration for the position. There are five ECQs: ECQ 1: Commitment to the Rule of Law and the Principles of the American Founding - This core qualification requires a demonstrated knowledge of the American system of government, commitment to uphold the Constitution and the rule of law, and commitment to serve the American people. ECQ 2: Driving Efficiency - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to strategically and efficiently manage resources, budget effectively, cut wasteful spending, and pursue efficiency through process and technological upgrades. ECQ 3: Merit and Competence - This core qualification involves the demonstrated knowledge, ability and technical competence to effectively and reliably produce work that is of exceptional quality. ECQ 4: Leading People - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to lead and inspire a group toward meeting the organization's vision, mission, and goals, and to drive a high-performance, high-accountability culture. This includes, when necessary, the ability to lead people through change and to hold individuals accountable. ECQ 5: Achieving Results - This core qualification involves the demonstrated ability to achieve both individual and organizational results, and to align results to stated goals from superiors. Note: If you are a member of the SES or have been certified through successful participation in an OPM approved SES Candidate Development Program (SESCDP), or have SES reinstatement eligibility, you do not need to respond to the ECQs. Instead, you should attach proof (e.g., SF-50, Certification by OPM's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB)) of your eligibility for noncompetitive appointment to the SES.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located in the Office of Health Technology and Products (OHTP) at the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS). As the Deputy Director and Chief Technology Officer, you will provide executive leadership, direction, and oversight for enterprise technology strategy, engineering, technical architecture, platform modernization, and emerging technology initiatives that support CMS's mission and strategic objectives.
Details.SubAgencyName: Office of Health Technology and Products
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Become a part of the Department that touches the lives of every American! At the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) you can give back to your community, state, and country by making a difference in the lives of Americans everywhere. Join HHS and help to make our world healthier, safer and better for all Americans. The Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services works in partnership with the entire health care community to improve quality and efficiency in an evolving health care system and provides leadership in the broader health care marketplace. Our effectiveness depends on the capabilities of a dedicated, professional staff that is committed to supporting these objectives. A career with CMS offers the opportunity to get involved on important national health care issues and be part of a dynamic, fast-paced, and highly visible organization. HHS has a critical preparedness and response mission: HHS protects the American people from health threats, researches emerging diseases, and mobilizes public health programs with domestic and international partners. In support of this mission, HHS offers its employees the opportunity to contribute their unique skills through voluntary temporary assignments to humanitarian emergencies or Departmental priorities countering new and emerging health, safety, and security threats.
MajorDuties: Establishes and directs the enterprise technical architecture, engineering standards, technology policies, and platform strategy for CMS digital services.

Directs enterprise build, buy, and integration strategies for shared capabilities: FHIR APIs, digital identity, fraud prevention and detection technologies, enterprise data platforms, cloud services, and AI infrastructure.
Leads enterprise engineering, technical architecture, and product technology strategy in partnership with the Chief Information Officer (CIO).
Serves as the agency's senior technical representative in government-wide and interagency forums.
Acts on behalf of the OHTP Director in matters involving technology strategy, architecture, engineering, and platform operations.
Advised senior CMS and Department leadership on emerging technologies, enterprise modernization priorities, digital transformation initiatives, and strategic investments.
Details.Evaluations: You will be evaluated on the quality and extent of your total accomplishments, experience, and education (if applicable). Your application will be rated and ranked by a Senior Executive Service (SES) Panel, comprised of at least three SES members, using only the information required within the application package. Applicants who do not demonstrate in their application sufficient possession of the ECQs and TQs will be determined ineligible for further consideration. Once the application process is complete, a review of your resume and supporting documentation will be conducted. If you meet minimum qualifications, your Application Package will be further reviewed to determine if you possess the Executive Core Qualifications (ECQ) and Technical Qualifications (TQ) listed above. ECQs and TQs must be thoroughly addressed within your two (2) page resume. Separate narratives will not be accepted or reviewed. Highly Qualified applicants may undergo one or more interviews and may be referred to the selecting official for further consideration. Upon selection, if not already a member of the SES serving under a career appointment, the individual selected must have his/her executive qualifications certified by the U.S. Office of Personnel Management's SES Qualifications Review Board (QRB) before appointment to this position. The selected individual's application will be forwarded to the OPM for review and certification by the QRB, unless the selectee provides evidence of noncompetitive status (e.g., a current SES, an OPM QRB-certified SESCDP graduate, or SES reinstatement eligibility). Upon QRB certification, the selected individual will be required to serve a one-year probationary period. For more information regarding the SES, go to https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/senior-executive-service/.

Details.OtherInformation: Veterans Preference: Veterans' preference is not applicable to the SES. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: DHS is calling on those who want to help protect American interests and secure our Nation. DHS Components work collectively to prevent terrorism; secure borders and our transportation systems; protect the President and other dignitaries; enforce and administer immigration laws; safeguard cyberspace; and ensure resilience to disasters. The DHS Joint Duty Program (JDP) is an intra- and inter-departmental program which offers civilian personnel professional and developmental opportunities. Joint Duty Assignments (JDAs) enhance operations and mission execution through unity of effort and collaboration. The DHS JDP is a human capital program initiative which is managed by OCHCO at DHS headquarters. The DHS JDP's purpose is two-fold: to encourage and to facilitate assignments of DHS personnel to other DHS components as well as outside agencies. The purpose of JDAs is to gain multi-component, multi-faceted experience focused on cross-cutting DHS and Federal-wide operations to enhance performance of the individual, the organizations, and the Department. JDAs are for a period not to exceed 1 year and do not qualify for Joint Duty credit. The DHS JDP covers current Federal employees at the GS-12 through GS-15 grade levels and equivalent. The DHS JDP does not apply to members of the military service or contractors. JDAs do not offer Temporary Promotions.
MajorDuties: Serve as a senior IT cybersecurity specialist responsible for advancing the DHS Intelligence Enterprise cybersecurity posture by applying security engineering best practices across IT networks, systems, applications, and multi-cloud environments. Provide expert guidance on Zero Trust, AI/ML, cloud security, risk management, security automation, and cybersecurity tools while collaborating with technical teams and advising leadership on security risks, requirements, and strategic improvements.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: To qualify for pay band 3A applicants must meet the following: Qualifying experience for Pay Band 3A includes one year of specialized experience (comparable to the Pay Band 3B or GS-14 or equivalent non-federal experience), which is directly related to the work of this position, and which has equipped the applicant with the knowledge, skills, and abilities to successfully perform the duties of the position. For this position, examples of specialized experience are: leading or overseeing day cybersecurity operations, such as security monitoring, threat detection, incident response, threat hunting, vulnerability management, and cyber defense activities; experience with enterprise cybersecurity technologies, such as Security Information and Event Management (SIEM), Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), vulnerability scanning, security analytics, automation, and cloud security capabilities; serving as the senior technical lead during cybersecurity incidents and coordinating detection, analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, forensic support, and lessons learned activities; overseeing security of a mid-scale, multi-platform information system, with geographically dispersed staff, involving Internet/Intranet/Extranet Systems, government owned/contractor operated GOGO systems, application servers, file servers, and local and wide area networks; coordinating cyber defense activities and integrating threat intelligence, adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures (TTPs), and emerging threat information into security operations; and conveying complex IT concepts clearly in both oral and written formats. Note: This experience MUST be well documented within your resume or application. In addition to meeting the specialized experience requirement, you must also have IT-related experience demonstrating each of the competencies listed below. Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive theservices or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work inthe agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide Decision Making - Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change. Information Management - Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems. Interpersonal Skills - Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends ton on verbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Teamwork- Has the capability to encourage and facilitate cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit, and works collaboratively with others to achieve shared goals. Technical Competence- Uses knowledge acquired through formal training or extensive on-the-job experience to perform your job. Works with, understands, and evaluates technical information related toyour role, and advising others on technical issues. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit may be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. To receive credit you must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours worked per week. A new hire's direct and overall experience are critical factors in determining a salary offer. It is important that your resume fully reflects all of your directly-related work experience. Salary offers include three key factors: The selectee's directly related experience at the same level as the position. The selectee's overall experience in a particular area. Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: If you are looking to be a part of a dynamic team environment then MCC is the place for you! Visit our Website at http://www.mcc.gov to see the life changing projects that our staffs are undertaking. The Millennium Challenge Corporation is an independent U.S. government agency focused on advancing America's economic and strategic interests through results-driven foreign assistance. MCC's grants support large-scale infrastructure, strategic reforms, and economic modernization. MCC delivers measurable returns to both recipients and U.S. taxpayers -expanding commercial opportunities for U.S. businesses, reducing the influence of competitors, and reinforcing global environments aligned with American values. Our model is defined by core principles, of selectivity, country ownership, transparency, and a focus on results. MCC Values are CLEAR: Embrace Collaboration, Always Learn, Practice Excellence, Be Accountable and Respect individuals and ideas. These values define how we behave as individuals and as an institution in pursuit of our mission. They guide how we make decisions, set priorities, address challenges, manage tradeoffs, recruit and develop staff, and work together with our country partners and stakeholders. Candidates should be committed to improving the efficiency of the Federal government, passionate about the ideals of our American republic, and committed to upholding the rule of law and the United States Constitution.
MajorDuties: Provides leadership and oversight for day-to-day cybersecurity operations, including security monitoring, threat detection, incident response, threat hunting, vulnerability management, and cyber defense activities. Oversees the operation and continuous improvement of enterprise cybersecurity technologies, including Security Information and Event Management (SIEM), Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR), vulnerability scanning, security analytics, automation, and cloud security capabilities. Directs enterprise vulnerability management activities, including prioritization and remediation of vulnerabilities, known exploited vulnerabilities (KEVs), and security weaknesses identified through assessments, audits, and continuous monitoring. Leads cybersecurity engineering efforts to design, implement, and maintain secure enterprise architectures aligned with Zero Trust principles. Oversee cybersecurity modernization initiatives involving Zero Trust architecture, cloud transformation, security automation, artificial intelligence-enabled cybersecurity capabilities, and advanced analytics. Serves as the senior technical lead during cybersecurity incidents and coordinates detection, analysis, containment, eradication, recovery, forensic support, and lessons learned activities. Reviews enterprise cybersecurity risks and provides technical recommendations to senior executives and system owners to support risk-based decision-making. Coordinates with internal and external stakeholders, including CISA, Inspectors General, auditors, federal partners, and cloud service providers to address cybersecurity risks, compliance requirements, and emerging threats. Establishes cybersecurity performance metrics, dashboards, and reporting mechanisms to communicate operational readiness, threat trends, vulnerabilities, and overall security posture to executive leadership. Coordinates with OCIO and Contracts and Grant Management staff on acquisition planning, strategy, and execution. Responsible for contract oversight and management, functioning as a contracting officer's representative (COR) or project manager (PM) on multiple contracts (as applicable) Performs other related duties as assigned.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite! USPACFLT is headquartered at Pearl Harbor on the island of Oahu in Hawaii, this four-star command is the world's largest fleet command. Encompassing 100 million square miles, our 200 ships/submarines, nearly 1,200 aircraft, and more than 130,000 uniformed and civilian Sailors serve on nearly half of the Earth's surface -- from Antarctica to the Arctic Circle, and from the U.S. West Coast to the Indian Ocean. Join the USPACFLT team to achieve more and to help protect and defend the maritime interests of the U.S. in the Indo-Pacific, providing combat-ready forces and operating forward, ready to fight tonight. We want talent and enthusiasm aboard the USPACFLT team. We want the best! For further information, please visit https://www.cpf.navy.mil/.
MajorDuties: You will use professional digital scanning, photogrammetry and editing software to produce, process, correct, model and modify point cloud data, for ship architectural records, active projects, simulations, education and communication.
You will analyze and optimize images with local changes or measurements, geometric manipulation or image alterations.
You will build scripts in software for automating image processing and data analysis or capture.

You will prepare finished 3D imagery for distribution t a variety of business interests, including ship architecture, project visualization, historic preservation, building information management and Building Information Modeling (BIM).
You will use computers to edit and manipulate 3D imagery 360 imagery, and remote capture imagery to produce special products for us by engineers in planning projects.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: GS-12 Your resume must demonstrate at least one year of specialized experience at or equivalent to the GS-11 grade level or pay band in the Federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector. Specialized experience must demonstrate the following: Experience serving as a Subject Matter Expert in overall Information Technology (IT) to support complex IT projects. Experience at the advanced level managing data storage, including optimization of hardware and software and administration. Experience utilizing the latest Windows Active Directory Infrastructure, including Group Policy administration, Domain Admin maintenance, and Domain Name System maintenance. Experience with state-of-the-art backup Implementation architecture and maintaining enterprise backup architecture using enterprise tools. Experience with the latest Virtual Server and Workstation software/hardware infrastructure such as VMWARE ESX, Windows Hyper-V, or VMWARE VDI. In addition to my experience demonstrating the four competencies above, I have one year of specialized experience equivalent to the next lower grade level (GS-09) or pay band in the federal service or equivalent experience in the private or public sector: Experience applying fundamental principles and practices for Windows Active Directory Infrastructure, including Group Policy Administration and DNS maintenance. Experience with state-of-the-art backup implementation and maintaining enterprise backup architecture using enterprise tools, such as Rubrik (RSC-P) Rubrik Security Cloud. Experience with Network Attached Storage (NAS), Storage Area Networks (SANS), and other network devices, such as NetApp (ONTAP). Experience with fundamental knowledge of RedHat and or Unix, including command line input. Experience with the latest Virtual Server and Workstation software/hardware infrastructure such as VMWARE ESX, Windows Hyper-V, or VMWARE VDI. Additional qualification information can be found from the following Office of Personnel Management website: https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/2200/information-technology-it-management-series-2210-alternative-a/ OR https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/classification-qualifications/general-schedule-qualification-standards/2200/information-technology-it-management-series-2210-alternative-b/ . Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as a IT SPECIALIST (SYSADMIN/INFOSEC) in the UNIX & Server Branch (10913), IT Infrastructure and Operations Division (1091), Information Technology & Cyber Security (ITACS) Office 109 of NORFOLK NAVAL SHIPYARD.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Navy and Marine Corps team offers innovative, exciting and meaningful work linking military and civilian talents to achieve our mission and safeguard our freedoms. Department of the Navy provides competitive salaries, comprehensive benefits, and extensive professional development and training. From pipefitters to accountants, scientists to engineers, doctors to nurses-the careers and opportunities to make a difference are endless. Civilian careers-where purpose and patriotism unite!
MajorDuties: You will ensure the rigorous application of information security/IA policies, principles, and practices in the delivery of workstation, server and storage services, network, and application and database IT services.

You will monitor and analyze applicable hardware and software resources and logs for issues, and recommending and implementing solutions that correct and improve conditions, and optimize efficiency of the system.
You will develop and implement procedures and guidelines to govern quality control and assurance of IT production operations.

You will analyze, diagnose, and correct recurring and emergency problems and faults with shipyard operating system’s software, hardware, and firmware, or initiate vendor corrective action, as appropriate, in order to restore normal operations.
You will ensure the rigorous application of information security/IA policies.
Details.Education: Education: All academic degrees and coursework must be from accredited or pre-accredited institutions. GS-11 Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree or 3 full years of progressively higher level graduate education leading to a Ph.D. or equivalent doctoral degree in computer science, engineering, information science, information systems management, mathematics, operations research, statistics, or technology management or degree that provided a minimum of 24 semester hours in one or more of the fields identified above and required the development or adaptation of applications, systems or networks.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: To qualify for the position of Chief Information Security Officer, at GS-2210-15, you must meet the basic qualification requirements listed below. To qualify for the GS-15 Chief Information Security Officer, applicants must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-14 level in the Federal service, performing duties such as: coordinating compliance and vulnerability remediation with IT stakeholders; providing expert technical advice and guidance on cybersecurity emerging technologies and modernization programs and practices; serving as an expert advisor on cybersecurity requirements and the protection of agency information and systems; participating in component and interagency project teams; analyzing technology trends and proposing solutions for technology challenges with broad government-wide implications; planning and overseeing component-wide IT projects involving innovative concepts and approaches; leading incident response efforts and promoting a culture of security awareness within the agency; providing protection capabilities including security event monitoring and investigations. You MUST meet all qualification requirements by the 11/30/2026 of this announcement. Your resume must support your responses to the application questionnaire and the qualification requirements. Failure to do so may result in an ineligible rating. See the Required Documents section for important notes about what must be included in your resume. Career Transition Programs (CTAP or ICTAP): These programs apply to Federal and/or DOJ employees who meet the definition of surplus or displaced from a position in the competitive service. To receive selection priority for this position, you must: Be rated well-qualified for the position based on the competencies; and submit the appropriate documentation to support your CTAP or ICTAP eligibility. Well-qualified is defined as having knowledge, skills, abilities, and/or competencies clearly exceeding the minimum qualification requirements for the vacancy.

Details.JobSummary: You will serve as the Civil Division's Chief Information Security Officer (CISO), responsible for overseeing the Division's information security strategy, policies, and implementation. You will provide authoritative direction and oversight of cybersecurity services within the Division. This position is being filled through Direct-Hire Authority (DHA) which is a hiring authority granted by the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) to address critical hiring needs or severe candidate shortages.
Details.SubAgencyName: Civil Division, Office of Information Technology
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Are you interested in a rewarding and challenging IT career? Join the U.S. Department of Justice, Civil Division! The Civil Division (Division) is the largest litigating component in the Department of Justice with approximately 2,000 employees and contractors. Each office within the Division handles cases worth millions, sometimes billions, of dollars, as well as cases that involve legal issues of great national importance, including matters of national security, separation of powers, and immigration. Come, be a part of a dynamic team that manages the Division's IT infrastructure, protects sensitive CIV data and systems from cyber threats, and promotes a culture of security awareness within the Division.
MajorDuties: The duties and responsibilities for a GS-15 Chief Information Security Officer position generally include, but are not limited to, the following: Serving as an expert advisor to attorneys, technology staff, litigation support, expert witnesses, and management on cybersecurity requirements related to litigation, claims, case and matters management technology requirements and the protection of Division information and systems. Assessing and conducting security reviews of enterprise and application architecture, software engineering, cloud-native delivery, software product lifecycles, continuous integration/continuous delivery methods, and digital playbook methods. Providing expert technical advice and guidance on cybersecurity emerging technologies and modernization programs and practices. Directing and coordinating compliance and vulnerability remediation with all IT stakeholders to prioritize remediation, solve any problems/blockers, and address gaps in cyber hygiene, network engineering, and system engineering practices. Planning and overseeing component-wide IT projects involving innovative concepts and approaches, particularly in scenarios where precedents are lacking, and multiple agencies and a large number of people are involved. Providing administrative and technical supervision necessary for completing the work of the unit. Observing workers' performance; conducting work performance critiques; providing advice and counsel to workers related to work and administrative matters.
Details.Evaluations: Once the job opportunity announcement closes (at 11:59 pm ET on 11/30/2026, your qualifications will be evaluated based on your application materials (e.g., resume, supporting documents) along with the results of the applied assessment. Qualified applicants who pass the assessment, which is used to determine proficiency, will be referred to the selecting official for consideration. The Hiring Official may select any qualified candidate. Veterans' preference is not applicable. Attention to Detail Customer Service Decision Making Information Management Information Resources Strategy and Planning Information Systems/Network Security Interpersonal Skills Leadership Oral Communication Problem Solving Project Management Teamwork Technical Competence When addressing the specialized experience statement, applicants must present evidence of the experience in their resume. If the specialized experience statement is repeated, in the applicant's resume, Human Resources will deem the applicant as ineligible. If you would like to preview the application questionnaire, please see: https://apply.usastaffing.gov/ViewQuestionnaire/13110192.
Details.HowToApply: To apply for this position, you must complete the online application questionnaire and submit your supporting documentation. Your complete application package must be submitted by 11:59 PM (EST) on 11/30/2026 to receive consideration. The application process is as follows: Click Apply to access the online application. You will need to be logged into your USAJOBS account to apply. If you do not have a USAJOBS account, you will need to create one before beginning the application. Follow the prompts to select your resume and/or other supporting documents to be included with your application package. You will have the opportunity to upload additional documents to include in your application before it is submitted. Your uploaded documents may take several hours to clear the virus scan process. After acknowledging you have reviewed your application package, complete the Include Personal Information section as you deem appropriate and click to continue with the application process. You will be taken to the online application which you must complete in order to apply for the position. Complete the online application, verify the required documentation is included with your application package, and submit the application. Essay Questions: The following four narrative questions provide an opportunity for you to highlight your dedication to public service for the hiring manager and agency leadership (or designee(s)). While your responses are not required and will not be scored, we encourage you to thoughtfully address each question. Please provide a response of 200 words or less to each question (see the application questionnaire). You will be asked to certify that you are using your own words and did not use a consultant or artificial intelligence (AI) such as a large language model (LLM) like ChatGPT or Copilot. How has your commitment to the Constitution and the founding principles of the United States inspired you to pursue this role within the Federal government? Provide a concrete example from professional, academic, or personal experience. In this role, how would you use your skills and experience to improve government efficiency and effectiveness? Provide specific examples where you improved processes, reduced costs, or improved outcomes. In this role, you will be expected to professionally and efficiently implement executive direction. Provide an example where you implemented leadership direction on a strategy or policy decision that differed from your own recommendation. How has a strong work ethic contributed to your professional, academic or personal achievements? Provide one or two specific examples, and explain how those qualities would enable you to serve effectively in this position. NEED HELP? If you need help with USAJOBs or the application process, please see the USAJOBS Help or Application Manager Online Help websites which includes information on managing your account, creating an application, uploading documents, etc. Reasonable Accommodation: To request reasonable accommodation for any part of the application and hiring process, please contact Victoria Jones at victoria.jones@usdoj.gov or 202-514-9048 for assistance.

However, you can also see your application status any time by logging in to your USAJOBS account and looking on the "Applications" page. Additional selections may be made from this announcement within 90 days.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: To evaluate your qualifications, your resume must clearly demonstrate how you meet the specialized experience described below. Your resume must not exceed two pages. To ensure your qualifications can be fully evaluated, we recommend including the following information: Name, address, telephone number, email address; Job Title (if Federal Service, provide series and grade; if not in GS plan, provide GS equivalent grade); Relevant work experience—should include employer name, job title, start and end dates (month/year), the number of hours worked per week and descriptions that explain how you meet the required qualifications in the job announcement. Education, certifications or licensures—If the job announcement requires any education, certifications or licensures, make sure to include the required information and any required documents like transcripts. Your resume should contain enough information to make a valid determination that you fully meet experience requirements for each grade level you are applying to. If you do not provide enough information for us to determine your qualifications, you may be rated ineligible If you have volunteered your service through a National Service program (e.g., Peace Corps, Americorps), we encourage you to apply and include this experience on your resume. The GS-13 salary range starts at $117,284 per year. If you are a new federal employee, your starting salary will likely be set at the Step 1 of the grade for which you are selected. To qualify, you must have at least one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 level or higher in the Federal service. Applicants applying for the GS-13 grade level must meet the following requirements: Have IT-related experience demonstrating EACH of the nine competencies AND one year of specialized experience equivalent to the GS-12 level in the Federal service as described below: Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Decision Making - Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change. Information Management - Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems. Interpersonal Skills - Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations. Oral Communication - This skill is generally demonstrated by assignments where the applicant persuades others to take a particular course of action or to accept findings, recommendations, changes, or alternative viewpoints. Problem Solving - This skill is generally demonstrated by assignments where the applicant identifies and accommodates technology and resource constraints. Teamwork - Encourages and facilitates cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit; works with others to achieve goals. Technical Competence – Uses knowledge that is acquired through formal training or on-the-job experience to perform one's job; works with, understands, and evaluates technical information related to the job; advises others on technical issues. To qualify, you must have one (1) year of specialized experience. Specialized experience is defined as ALL of the following: Contributing to an agile team in developing, testing, debugging, and maintaining digital products and services for public-facing or enterprise environments, including data engineering, cloud-native architectures, computer hardware/software integration, cybersecurity-by-design, performance requirements, interoperability, and/or secure deployment of emerging technologies. This includes applying modern programming languages, frameworks, and technologies (e.g., Python, Go, JavaScript, TypeScript, Node.js, React, Ruby on Rails, Terraform, Next.js, HTML/CSS, Rust). Contributing to the end-to-end design, development, and deployment of digital products, systems and solutions by integrating emergent technologies and industry best practices. Applying information security and privacy best practices and performing risk assessments in artificial intelligence or cloud environments

Details.JobSummary: As an Al Software Engineer you will establish technical strategies, standards, and architectures to drive secure, ethical, and engineering-sound AI adoption across the federal government. This position is with the Office of Technology Transformation Services (TTS), Federal Acquisition Service (FAS), General Services Administration (GSA). We are currently filling multiple vacancies, but additional vacancies may be filled as needed.
MajorDuties: Serves as a principal technical expert formulating and directing high level, enterprise-wide engineering strategies for Al-enabled systems, computer hardware/software integration, and cloud-native architectures and platforms, delivering impactful solutions for the American people. Provides technical guidance for the development and management of Al-enabled systems, computer hardware/software integration, and cloud-native architectures, ensuring compliance with federal mandates, executive orders, and/or other guidelines. Serves as a strategic authority on Al, data strategy and emerging technologies in collaboration with stakeholders and partners. Provides authoritative consultation and technical guidance to agency personnel, shaping national and international Al, computer engineering and digital policies, directives and mandates. Provides expert IT advice to generate and develop new guidance and direction related to efficiency and effectiveness of mission-critical programs and technology solutions and services within customer agencies. Formulates implementation strategies and policies for agency and governmentwide application. The Technology Transformation Services (TTS) is responsible for providing scalable software products and services to federal agencies.
Details.Requirements: If selected, you must meet the following conditions: Current or Former Political Appointees: The Office of Personnel Management (OPM) must authorize employment offers made to current or former political appointees. If you are currently, or have been within the last 5 years, a political Schedule A, Schedule C or Non­Career SES employee in the Executive Branch, you must disclose this information to the HR Office. Failure to disclose this information could result in disciplinary action including removal from Federal Service. Position security requirements are dependent on the position for which selected, and may be designated at Top Secret, Secret, High Risk, Moderate Risk or Low Risk. Dependent on which position you are selected for you will be required to undergo and pass the appropriate Tier background investigation level. You must be granted this clearance before you can start the job. Have your identity and work status eligibility verified if you are not a GSA employee. We will use the Department of Homeland Security's e-Verify system for this. Any discrepancies must be resolved as a condition of continued employment. Any applicant tentatively selected for this position will be required to submit to urinalysis to screen for illegal drug use prior to appointment. Appointment to the position will be contingent upon a negative drug test result. Some positions may require to perform on-call duty outside typical schedule duty hours as needed and directed to respond to and resolve issues related to fraud, platform, engineering, partnership, and/or other comparable issues. Serve a one year probationary period, if required.
Details.Evaluations: Your application will be evaluated against the basic qualifications which includes any specialized experience and/or education requirements (if applicable). Qualified candidates will be considered in accordance with the Office of Personnel Management Direct Hire Guidelines. Applications will not be rated or ranked. Veterans' Preference is not applicable to the direct hire recruitment procedures. Failure to submit a complete application or missing required supporting documentation may result in you not being considered for the position. Falsification of your background, education, and/or experience is grounds for non-selection or dismissal if hired. Technical Assessment: Shortly after the job posting closes, eligible applicants will receive an email with a link to a technical assessment to complete. Responses to the assessment will be used to measure the depth of knowledge in relation to the required competencies for the position. Candidates who pass the assessment will move to the next phase. Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) Resume Review: Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) will review your resume to determine your technical qualifications for this position based on the required competencies, including the required IT competencies and the specialized experience on a pass/fail process. ICTAP/CTAP Candidates: The Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan (ICTAP) and Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP) provide eligible displaced Federal competitive service employees with selection priority over other candidates for competitive service vacancies. To be qualified you must submit appropriate documentation (a copy of the agency notice, your most recent performance rating, and your most recent SF-50 noting current position, grade level, and duty location) and be found “well-qualified" for this vacancy. In addition to meeting the basic qualifications stated in the qualification section of this announcement, well qualified is defined as: experience that exceeds the minimum qualifications of the position, demonstrated by meeting at least 3 out of 5 KSA's listed below: Ability to establish and communicate technical standards, Al engineering policies, and architectures for the ethical, secure, and trustworthy use of Al and emerging technologies. Ability to apply IT specialty interrelationships, agency IT architecture, emerging technologies, new IT developments, business process applications, and IT security concepts, standards, and methods. Ability to make recommendations and provide input for major decisions that may significantly influence important agency IT policies or programs. Ability to provide expert technical advice, guidance, and recommendations to management and other technical specialists on critical IT issues. Ability to apply advanced IT principles, concepts, methods, standards, and practices sufficient to accomplish assignments such as: develop and interpret policies, procedures, and strategies governing the planning and delivery of services throughout the agency. Demonstration of these KSA's must be supported by your resume. You may preview questions for this vacancy.
