MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: To qualify at the GS-13 grade level, your resume must demonstrate at least one (1) full year of specialized experience equivalent to at least the GS-12 grade level in the federal or private sector. Specialized experience is experience that has equipped you with the ability, skill, and knowledge to successfully perform the duties of this position and is typically in or related to this line of work. Examples of specialized experience include performing the following types of tasks on a regular basis. NOTE: All experience statements (i.e., duties, specialized experience, or occupational assessment questionnaire) copied from this announcement and pasted into your resume will not be considered as a demonstration of your qualifications for this position. Specialized experience must include the following: Leading the development, operation, and maintenance of standardized, consistent, and efficient software developer environments, platform pipelines, and delivery workflows across an enterprise software organization. Managing a centralized developer interface or platform to facilitate team interaction with cloud services; and delivering enablement capabilities such as self-service tooling, technical documentation, and workflows designed to reduce friction and accelerate secure software delivery. Establishing and managing structured onboarding programs, developer support resources, and technical training to enable rapid, secure adoption of software development platforms and cloud capabilities. Analyzing developer feedback, system usage patterns, and delivery performance metrics to drive continuous improvements to developer tools, workflows, and platform environments. Supervising and leading a team of software developers, engineers, or DevSecOps specialists, including managing workload priorities, evaluating performance, and implementing equal employment opportunity (EEO) policies. In addition to meeting the specialized experience requirement, you must also have IT-related experience demonstrating each of the competencies listed below. Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Decision Making - Makes sound, well-informed, and objective decisions; perceives the impact and implications of decisions; commits to action, even in uncertain situations, to accomplish organizational goals; causes change. Information Management - Identifies a need for and knows where or how to gather information; organizes and maintains information or information management systems. Interpersonal Skills - Shows understanding, friendliness, courtesy, tact, empathy, concern, and politeness to others; develops and maintains effective relationships with others; may include effectively dealing with individuals who are difficult, hostile, or distressed; relates well to people from varied backgrounds and different situations. Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Teamwork- Has the capability to encourage and facilitate cooperation, pride, trust, and group identity; fosters commitment and team spirit, and works collaboratively with others to achieve shared goals. Technical Competence- Uses knowledge acquired through formal training or extensive on-the-job experience to perform your job. Works with, understands, and evaluates technical information related to your role, and advising others on technical issues. NOTE: Education cannot be substituted for experience at this grade level. National Service Experience (i.e., volunteer experience): Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional, philanthropic, religious, spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

Details.JobSummary: This vacancy is for a GS-2210-13, Supervisory IT Cybersecurity Specialist (PLCYPLN-INFOSEC) located in the Department of Homeland Security, U.S. Coast Guard, C5ISC INFRASTRUCTURE SERVICES DIVISION in ALEXANDRIA, Virginia.
Details.SubAgencyName: C5ISC, Cloud and Data Branch, DATA Infrastructure Section
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) is calling on those who want to help protect American interests and secure our Nation. DHS Components work collectively to prevent terrorism; secure borders and our transportation systems; protect the President and other dignitaries; enforce and administer immigration laws; safeguard cyberspace; and ensure resilience to disasters. We achieve these vital missions through a workforce spanning hundreds of occupations. Make an impact; join DHS. Apply for this exciting position to support U.S. Coast Guard (USCG) missions of safeguarding our Nation's maritime interests in the heartland, in the ports, at sea, and around the globe.
MajorDuties: You will serve as an Supervisory IT Cybersecurity Specialist (PLCYPLN-INFOSEC) and be responsible for managing information technology projects. Being a Coast Guard civilian makes you a valuable member of the Coast Guard team. Typical work assignments include: Directing, managing, and monitoring complex IT projects, including evaluating project costs, design changes, and resource requirements.. Evaluating risk, compliance, and assurance efforts; monitoring and auditing National Security Systems (NSS) and coordinating system security certification and accreditation (RMF/ATO processes).. Leading contracting, procurement, and budget oversight; evaluates supply chain risk (NIST SP 800-161) and ensures cybersecurity requirements are integrated into contracts. Supervising a multidisciplinary team across various locations; manages performance, reviews resumes, conducts interviews, executes EEO policies, and plans employee training Providing expert advice on capital planning regulations (e.g., Clinger-Cohen Act) and collaborates/negotiates with external agencies (DoD, DHS, OMB) on government-wide policy initiatives. Managing and secures data pipeline systems, data lakes, and Coast Guard data fabric; defines and monitors Service-Level Agreements (SLAs) and Operating Level Agreements (OLAs). Mandatory training is required which must be successfully completed and other training may occur as necessary for success in the position. A. Federal Acquisition Certification for Program and Project Managers Level II (FAC P/PM-II) or management determined equivalent within two years of entry into the position. B. Information Assurance Management Level II (IAM-II) or management determined equivalent within two years of entry into the position. Reasonable Accommodation (RA) Requests: If you believe you have a disability (i.e., physical or mental), covered by the Rehabilitation Act of 1973 as amended that would interfere with completing the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, you will be granted the opportunity to request a RA in your online application. Requests for RA for the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments and appropriate supporting documentation for RA must be received prior to starting the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments. Decisions on requests for RA are made on a case-by-case basis. If you meet the minimum qualifications of the position, after notification of the adjudication of your request, you will receive an email invitation to complete the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments, based on your adjudication decision. You must complete all assessments within 48 hours of receiving the URL to access the USA Hire Competency Based Assessments if you received the link after the close of the announcement. MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: CYBER EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITIONS ARE NOT SUBJECT TO THE TWO-PAGE RESUME LIMIT. YOUR FULL RESUME WILL NEED TO BE UPLOADED TO YOUR USAJOBS PROFILE USING THE DOCUMENT TYPE "OTHER DOCUMENTS". This position is in the Professional Work Category at the Full Performance Work Level within the CES Occupational Structure. Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Current Civilian Employees of the Organization Applying to Cyber Excepted Service (CES) Positions Organization is defined as current, permanent ARCYBER/NETCOM employees only. Army CES positions apply Veteran's Preference to preference eligible candidates, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 3005, "CES Employment and Placement". If you are a veteran claiming veterans' preference, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must submit documents verifying your eligibility with your application package. In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. To qualify based on your experience, your resume must describe one year of applicable experience that demonstrates the possession of knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Such experience is typically in or directly related to the work of the position to be filled. Specialized experience would be demonstrated by organizing risk management framework authorization efforts by preparing security documentation to include updating system inventories and coordinating routine control reviews to maintain compliance with established requirements; observing cybersecurity vulnerabilities by validating basic remediation actions to help reduce recurring weaknesses across assigned systems; collaborating in cybersecurity risk analysis by drafting preliminary risk summaries that informed leadership on potential mission impacts. My experience includes, or was supplemented by, information technology related experience (paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training, as appropriate) which demonstrates each of the four competencies, as defined: (1) Attention to Detail Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: Complete thorough and accurate work independently, even in the most difficult or stressful situations. Occasionally review work completed by others; (2) Customer Service Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: resolve routine and non-routine problems, questions, or complaints. Develop and maintain strong, mutually supportive working relationships with customers. Conduct evaluation of support to determine quality of services and customer satisfaction, and recommend procedural changes based on customer need or changes in policy and/or regulation; (3) Oral Communication Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: convincingly convey complex information to customers. Present thoughts that are well- organized and demonstrate confidence in the facts and ideas. Adjust style when working with individuals with different levels of understanding; use various methods to explain and convey information; and (4) Problem Solving Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: solve complex or sensitive problems by developing and proposing strategic alternatives. Identify possible conflicts and shared benefits. Help team anticipate problems and identify and evaluate potential sources of information; provide feedback and coaching to others to help solve problems. Engage appropriate stakeholders when developing solutions in order to understand and incorporate multiple perspectives and needs. Evaluate the effectiveness of decisions and adjust future decisions as appropriate.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Qualifications required: Expertise in integrating automated security controls, including SAST, DAST, SCA, and Infrastructure-as-Code scanning, into CI/CD pipelines while enabling rapid and secure software delivery. Experience with vulnerability management, security tool optimization, and software supply chain security practices is essential. Advanced proficiency administering and securing enterprise development platforms such as GitHub, GitHub Actions, CloudBees/Jenkins, JFrog Artifactory, and ArgoCD. This includes implementing repository governance, secrets management, access controls, build automation, GitOps workflows, and artifact security. Strong experience with Terraform, CloudFormation, Kubernetes, containers, and cloud environments is required to support secure cloud and application deployment practices. Hands-on experience with cloud and application security platforms such as Wiz, Prisma Cloud, and Checkmarx, including cloud security posture management, application security testing, and container security. Should be capable of serving as a technical lead, providing strategic guidance to development and security teams, advancing secure-by-design principles, and driving enterprise-wide improvements in DevSecOps maturity and software supply chain resilience Please read the following important information to ensure we have everything we need to consider your application: It is your responsibility to ensure that you submit appropriate documentation prior to the closing date. Details.JobSummary: 6-12 month non-reimbursable assignment. The only compensation for this assignment is the federal salary you are already receiving. Resumes are reviewed every 30 days until selection/closing date. This is a Detail, not a Developmental Rotation. Supervisory approval form must be signed.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: DHS is calling on those who want to help protect American interests and secure our Nation. DHS Components work collectively to prevent terrorism; secure borders and our transportation systems; protect the President and other dignitaries; enforce and administer immigration laws; safeguard cyberspace; and ensure resilience to disasters. The DHS Joint Duty Program (JDP) is an intra- and inter-departmental program which offers civilian personnel professional and developmental opportunities. Joint Duty Assignments (JDAs) enhance operations and mission execution through unity of effort and collaboration. The DHS JDP is a human capital program initiative which is managed by OCHCO at DHS headquarters. The DHS JDP's purpose is two-fold: to encourage and to facilitate assignments of DHS personnel to other DHS components as well as outside agencies. The purpose of JDAs is to gain multi-component, multi-faceted experience focused on cross-cutting DHS and Federal-wide operations to enhance performance of the individual, the organizations, and the Department. JDAs are for a period not to exceed 1 year and do not qualify for Joint Duty credit. The DHS JDP covers current Federal employees at the GS-12 through GS-15 grade levels and equivalent. The DHS JDP does not apply to members of the military service or contractors. JDAs do not offer Temporary Promotions.
MajorDuties: Provides technical leadership for cloud and application security platforms including Prisma Cloud, Wiz, and Checkmarx. Conducts cloud security posture assessments, application security testing, container and Kubernetes security reviews, and vulnerability analysis. Evaluates and prioritizes security findings, reduces false positives, and delivers actionable remediation guidance to development and platform engineering teams Supports enterprise artifact management and GitOps-based deployment practices by securing software supply chains, managing binary repositories, implementing vulnerability scanning and signature verification, and ensuring secure synchronization of code and infrastructure across cloud-native environments. Collaborates with cross-functional stakeholders to strengthen cyber resilience, improve secure-by-design engineering practices, and advance organizational DevSecOps maturity. Provide enterprise DevSecOps, cloud security, and secure software delivery expertise across development, security, and operations teams. Leads the integration of automated security controls into CI/CD pipelines, ensuring the continuous enforcement of security policies through automated scanning, vulnerability management, and Infrastructure as Code (IaC) validation while maintaining development velocity. Administers and secures enterprise software development and delivery platforms, including GitHub, GitHub Actions, CloudBees/Jenkins, Artifactory, and ArgoCD. Develops, configures, and maintains secure build and deployment pipelines, repository governance, access controls, secrets management, and shared automation frameworks that enable consistent and compliant software releases.

Basic Requirements: Attention to Detail- experience reviewing my own information technology-related work or data and have been asked by others to review their work or data to ensure accuracy, completeness, and consistency with standards Customer Service - experience maintaining relationships with customers, assessing current information technology needs of customers, and developing or identifying information technology products and services that are tailored to meet customer needs Oral Communication -briefing mid-level management and IT staff on the status of information technology systems, projects, or daily operations, including the communication of technical information to a non-technical audience Problem Solving - identifying alternatives to address complex information technology-related issues by gathering and applying information from a variety of sources that provide a number of potential solutions Qualifying Experience: In addition to meeting the basic requirement, applicants must possess qualifying experience. To qualify based on your experience, your resume must describe at least one year of experience that demonstrates the competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Experience refers to any paid or unpaid experience, including volunteer work and Military service, that would be considered equivalent to work normally performed at the next lower grade level in the federal service. For this position, qualifying experience is defined as: Experience as a system administrator of cloud-based environments. Experience with installing, configuring, and maintaining operating systems in alignment with an organization's IT framework to meet critical business needs. Volunteer Experience: Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual, community, student, social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge, and skills and can provide valuable training and experience that translates to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Candidates must describe how they meet the qualifying experience and/or selective placement factor(s) within the body of their resume. All qualifications must be met within 30 days after the closing date of the announcement. **Combination of education and experience is not applicable for this position.**

It has been identified as a position necessary to carry out and support the mission of the US Cyber Command. It is in the PROFESSIONAL Work Category at the FULL PERFORMANCE Work Level within the CES Occupational Structure. It is located in the DISA - HC/Mainframe LOB-Multiple Agencies .
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: If you want to do interesting and challenging work and to make a contribution to national defense, DISA is a great place for you.DISA provides secure and reliable communications and computing support that enable the President and our military forces to communicate globally through voice, video, and data transmission. DISA is a leader within the Federal Government in implementing "people programs" and offers a broad range of quality-of-life and training programs. Go to www.disa.mil for more information. This position is in the Excepted Service and does NOT convey eligibility to be converted to the Competitive Service. It is being recruited under 10 U.S.C. 1599f into the Cyber Excepted Service (CES) personnel system. Positions in the Cyber Excepted Service are positions necessary to carry out and support the mission of the United States Cyber Command.
MajorDuties: Collaborate on installing, configuring, and maintaining servers, software, and essential IT infrastructure. Contribute to data security and availability by actively participating in daily backup and recovery system operation.
Work with teams on the optimal design, deployment, and management of cloud resources across platforms.
Gather information and report findings about cloud provisioning, configuration, and maintenance practices. Monitor cloud resources and report any performance issues for evaluation.

Participate in interagency teams and training opportunities to stay informed about emerging technological trends. Maintain awareness of DoD's objectives and best practices through assigned tasks and communication.

Gather information and report findings about technology vendors and products. Participate in training opportunities to stay informed about the latest IT trends. Contribute to the financial aspects of IT through assigned tasks.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: You must meet the following requirements by the closing date of this announcement. Specialized Experience: Specialized Experience for the GS-14, you must have one year (full 52 weeks) of specialized experience at a level of difficulty and responsibility equivalent to the GS-13 grade level in the Federal service. Specialized experience for this position is defined as: - Managing and maintaining enterprise virtual and physical server environments; AND - Administering and maintaining enterprise domain infrastructure, including at least two of the following: Server deployment and configuration, Active Directory, Group Policy, DNS, authentication services, replication, patch management, and vulnerability remediation; AND - Ensuring secure, reliable, and compliant enterprise infrastructure services across hybrid and cloud platforms; AND - Providing technical leadership, mentoring, and oversight to IT professionals; AND - Communicating to management on technical risks, resource requirements, infrastructure investments, modernization opportunities, or strategic improvements to enterprise IT operations. In addition to meeting specialized experience, individuals must meet proficiency levels in each of the following competencies: Attention to Detail, Customer Service, Decision Making, Information Management, Interpersonal Skills, Oral Communication, Problem Solving, Teamwork, and Technical Competence. A structured interview may be used to determine if you meet the required proficiency levels. You will be interviewed about past experience or hypothetical situations. For the required proficiency levels and competency definitions, please see the following link: Competency-Based Qualification Standard for the Information Technology Management Series, 2210 Time-in-Grade: In addition to the above requirements, you must meet the following time-in-grade requirement, if applicable: For the GS-14, you must have been at the GS-13 level for 52 weeks. Time After Competitive Appointment: Candidates who are current Federal employees serving on a non-temporary competitive appointment must have served at least three months in that appointment.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located at Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration,Office of Information Technology. As a System Administrator, you will be a senior level information technology specialist serving as a subject matter expert on specialized information technologies and their role within TIGTA's enterprise architecture.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The United States (U.S.) Department of the Treasury (Treasury) has a distinguished history dating back to the founding of our nation. As the steward of U.S. economic and financial systems, Treasury is a major and influential leader in today's global economy. TIGTA reports to the Secretary of the Treasury and is charged with providing independent oversight of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). TIGTA's work plays a major role in protecting the nation's revenue stream as we are committed to the prevention and detection of fraud, waste, and abuse within the IRS. We have over 700 employees located in offices across the country. Come Join the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration and Invest in Tomorrow.
MajorDuties: As a System Administrator, you will: Develops and implements migration strategies including planning for continuity of operations during the deployment of new server technology. Plans and coordinates the installation, configuration, maintenance, and upgrade of enterprise management software and related enterprise-level changes to the system infrastructure. Lead IT systems development projects from design to support. Evaluate the effectiveness of installed systems and services. Provide advice on and devises solutions to a wide range of IT issues. Derive organizational and system performance enhancements. Leads multi-functional development projects in software analysis, design, development, and implementation for a new system or major enhancement to an existing system. Provides authoritative advice to other specialists in areas such as disaster recovery, capacity planning, applications development, hardware strategy, and operating systems security. Leads major operating systems projects such as installation of new operating environments or implementation of new operating systems patches, upgrades, and releases. Lead in the development and implementation of workable approaches to IT architecture, capital investment planning, e-Government, and other IT related legislative and policy initiatives. Develop long-range plans for IT security systems that anticipate, identify, evaluate, mitigate, and minimize risks associated with IT systems vulnerabilities.

Details.Evaluations: You will be evaluated based on how well you meet the qualifications listed in this vacancy announcement. Your qualifications will be evaluated based on your application materials (e.g., résumé, supporting documents), the responses you provide on the application questionnaire, and the result of the online assessments required for this position. Please be sure that your résumé includes detailed information to support your qualifications for this position; failure to provide sufficient evidence in your résumé may result in a "not qualified" determination. In order to be considered for this position, you must complete all required steps in the process. In addition to the application and application questionnaire, this position requires an online assessment. The online assessment measures critical general competencies required to perform the job. Overstating your qualifications and/or experience in your application materials or application questionnaire may result in your removal from consideration. Cheating on the online assessment may also result in your removal from consideration. You will be assessed on the following competencies (knowledge, skills, abilities, and other characteristics): Accountability Attention to Detail Attention to Detail Customer Service Decision Making Decision Making Flexibility Influencing/Negotiating Information Management Integrity/Honesty Interpersonal Skills Interpersonal Skills Learning Oral Communication Problem Solving Reading Comprehension Reasoning Self-Management Stress Tolerance Teamwork Technical Competence The USA Hire Assessment includes a cut score based on the minimum level of required proficiency in these critical general competencies. You must meet or exceed the cut score to be considered. You will not be considered for the position if you score below the cut score or fail to complete the assessment. If you are a displaced or surplus Federal employee eligible for the Career Transition Assistance Plan (CTAP)/Interagency Career Transition Assistance Plan (ICTAP), achieve a well-qualified score of 85 or higher to receive priority consideration. When TIGTA completes its hiring, the remaining list of qualified candidates may be shared with additional Treasury bureaus. You will have an opportunity to opt-in if you would like your name, application material, and assessment results shared to be considered for employment with additional Treasury bureaus. There is no guarantee of further consideration, and you can continue to explore other job opportunity announcements.

Details.JobSummary: This position is located at Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration,Office of Information Technology. As a System Administrator, you will be a senior level information technology specialist serving as a subject matter expert on specialized information technologies and their role within TIGTA's enterprise architecture.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The United States (U.S.) Department of the Treasury (Treasury) has a distinguished history dating back to the founding of our nation. As the steward of U.S. economic and financial systems, Treasury is a major and influential leader in today's global economy. TIGTA reports to the Secretary of the Treasury and is charged with providing independent oversight of the Internal Revenue Service (IRS). TIGTA's work plays a major role in protecting the nation's revenue stream as we are committed to the prevention and detection of fraud, waste, and abuse within the IRS. We have over 700 employees located in offices across the country. Come Join the Treasury Inspector General for Tax Administration and Invest in Tomorrow.
MajorDuties: As a System Administrator, you will: Develops and implements migration strategies including planning for continuity of operations during the deployment of new server technology. Plans and coordinates the installation, configuration, maintenance, and upgrade of enterprise management software and related enterprise-level changes to the system infrastructure. Lead IT systems development projects from design to support. Evaluate the effectiveness of installed systems and services. Provide advice on and devises solutions to a wide range of IT issues. Derive organizational and system performance enhancements. Leads multi-functional development projects in software analysis, design, development, and implementation for a new system or major enhancement to an existing system. Provides authoritative advice to other specialists in areas such as disaster recovery, capacity planning, applications development, hardware strategy, and operating systems security. Leads major operating systems projects such as installation of new operating environments or implementation of new operating systems patches, upgrades, and releases. Lead in the development and implementation of workable approaches to IT architecture, capital investment planning, e-Government, and other IT related legislative and policy initiatives. Develop long-range plans for IT security systems that anticipate, identify, evaluate, mitigate, and minimize risks associated with IT systems vulnerabilities.

Details.JobSummary: This position is in the Department of the Chief Information Technology Officer, Information Technology Security Office (ITSO). ITSO manages the Judiciary's IT security program; protects the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of Judiciary information and systems; oversees enterprise security operations and incident response; develops national security policies and guidance; and works with Judiciary and external partners to safeguard IT operations and support the Judiciary's mission.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: The Administrative Office (AO) of the United States Courts supports, through excellence and innovation, the constitutional and statutory mission of the federal judiciary to provide equal justice under the law as an independent and equal branch of government. The AO, an agency of the judicial branch of the federal government, is committed to serving and supporting the federal court system of the United States. The AO provides a broad range of legislative, legal, financial, technology, management, administrative and program support services to the Federal courts. AO positions are classified and paid under a broad-banded system with the exception of positions in the AO Executive Service. Salary is commensurate with experience. Most AO employees are eligible for full federal and judiciary benefits. The AO is committed to attracting the best and brightest applicants in our support of the third branch of government. We take pride in serving the judicial branch and supporting its mission to provide equal justice under law.
MajorDuties: The IT Specialist (Security) serves as senior level Security Control Assessment subject-matter expert (SME) responsible for leading complex, enterprise-level assessments of security controls across information systems, applications, cloud and hybrid environments. The incumbent provides authoritative technical advice to senior management, Authorizing Officials, and other stakeholders on control effectiveness, security risk, systemic weaknesses, remediation, compensating controls, and residual risk. The selectee will also develop and improve assessment methods, procedures, testing approaches, and quality practices; resolve complex assessment issues; identify systemic and enterprise-wide weaknesses; and provide technical leadership to multidisciplinary assessment teams. The incumbent must also be able to perform the tasks and meet the requirements outlined in NIST Special Publication 800-181 National Initiative for Cybersecurity Education (NICE) Cybersecurity Workforce for the role of Security Control Assessment (OG-WRL-012). Duties Include: Leading complex security control assessments by planning, leading, and conducting enterprise-level assessments of information systems, applications, cloud and hybrid environments; establishing assessment scope, objectives, methodology, evidence requirements, and testing approaches based on system risk and mission impact. Serving as a senior technical authority and providing independent risk analysis; applying independent professional judgment to evaluate complex technical and security issues and developing risk-based recommendations without assuming risk-acceptance or authorization authority. Developing and improving security control assessment methodologies. Establishing appropriate assessment approaches for complex, emerging, and non-standard technology environments, including cloud, DevSecOps, and other modern architectures. Analyzing systemic and enterprise-level risk and resolve complex assessment issues. Resolving complex or contentious assessment issues involving disputed findings, conflicting evidence, control interpretations, compensating controls, and competing mission requirements and defend assessment conclusions and recommendations before senior technical and management officials. Leading multidisciplinary assessment teams and stakeholder engagement. Providing technical leadership and direction to assessment teams and coordinating assessment activities with system owners, architects, engineers, developers, cybersecurity and privacy personnel, contractors, and other subject-matter experts. Communicating assessment results and support authorization and risk management decisions. Developing clear, accurate, and defensible assessment reports, findings, briefings, and other decision-support materials. Driving continuous improvement of assessment practices. Evaluating lessons learned, assessment results, emerging threats, technology changes, and evolving security requirements to identify opportunities to improve assessment quality, efficiency, consistency, and risk-management decision support.

OCS administers wide-ranging elements of TM's regulatory program for clearing agencies, transfer agents, and other intermediaries. OCS administers TM's clearance and settlement program. OCS also works closely with other regulators and industry groups, on various legislative and regulatory initiatives.
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Our mission includes advocating for investors who seek to secure a future for their family, providing guidance and regulations for the nation's securities industry in an increasingly global market, and taking action with an eye toward promoting the capital formation necessary to sustain economic growth. A career with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) offers work that is exciting, challenging and rewarding. You can contribute to securities regulation and enforcement while making a positive difference for the American investing public. The SEC provides: Careers that broaden and deepen your already accomplished knowledge, skills and abilities; An environment that allows you to work and learn with the nation's experts; Benefits, compensation and career expansion opportunities; and A balance between your professional and family life. The SEC offers a number of enhanced pay and benefits plus the standard Federal benefits. Please be sure to visit the SEC's compensation and benefits program pages.
MajorDuties: In this role as a Senior Financial Analyst, you will be responsible for: Ongoing oversight of SRO operational risk, cybersecurity, and business continuity initiatives and reporting. Conducting periodic meetings with the SROs regarding such topics, including consulting with other regulators to develop an agenda, leading the meeting, and following up on outstanding topics. Reviewing and analyzing proposals from SROs related to proposed rule change filings by clearing agencies in the cash and derivatives markets, related to all aspects of a clearing agency's operations, including those related to operational risk, cybersecurity, business continuity, and cloud technology. Providing expert-level advice and consultation related to operational risk management, cyber security, and information technology as used by SROs to SEC staff. Also analyzing and developing reports, recommendations, and advice on regulatory developments affecting financial institutions including registered clearing agencies and other financial market infrastructures. Leading various OCS special projects as needed, including rulemaking initiatives. Preparing and presenting findings and recommendations to senior management within TM, to other offices, and the Chairman and Commissioners. Working closely with OCS attorneys, economists, and analysts, developing regulations and policy, and in connection with proposed rule changes by registered clearing agencies and other self-regulatory organizations involving OCS matters. Representing SEC in meetings, conferences and public forums; displaying current knowledge and understanding of policy issues related to the assigned segment of the market; maintaining productive work relationships with international, federal and state government agencies and the securities industry.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.SubAgency: Air Force Life Cycle Management Center
MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: Experience requirements are described in the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) Qualification Standards for General Schedule Positions, Professional and Scientific Positions. Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. In addition to meeting the basic requirement above, to qualify for this position you must also meet the qualification requirements listed in the Individual Occupational Requirements for Information Technology Specialists SPECIALIZED EXPERIENCE: Applicants must have IT-related experience demonstrating each of the following four competencies: Attention to Detail, Customer Service, Oral Communication, Problem Solving AND have, or within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement will have, at least 1 year (52 weeks) of specialized experience which is equivalent to Federal experience at the next lower grade (GS-11), level, pay band (NH-02), or equivalent (pay schedule, pay band, etc). Specialized experience is described as: Demonstrating proven expertise directing the Risk Management Framework (RMF) lifecycle within DoD cloud environments, securing DevSecOps pipelines and emerging AI/ML architectures, and orchestrating enterprise SIEM, threat hunting, and incident response operations. NOTE: Due to the use of 120-day rosters, this period of experience may be completed within 120 days of the closing date of this announcement. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (KSAs): Your qualifications will be evaluated on the basis of your level of knowledge, skills, abilities and/or competencies in the following areas: Duty 1: Responsible for the design, development, installation, test, implementation, modification, documentation and follow-up maintenance of systems software for the Kessel Run Experimental Lab (KREL). Performs in-depth analysis. This involves determining a need or responding to a stated need, identifying and evaluating available system software (if any) or guiding the writing of the software and monitoring other systems software programmers or contractor personnel in performance of test, implementation, modification, documentation and follow-up maintenance. Serves as technical expert performing analysis of automated and manual systems to accomplish design and programming assignment. Projects typically involve analyses of large, complex systems. Applies information systems security principles and methods to all functions. Performs consultation and research to determine common and unique requirements, to establish standardized terms and data elements for uniform identification by all users and to select and/or develop a system design to meet established standards. Duty 2: Serves as expert planner, analyst and advisor for data management. Serves as technical advisor to management, responsible for evaluating and providing recommendations of new database technologies and architectures and/or developing and administrating data standards, policies, and procedures. Diagnoses and resolves complex data management problems and issues. Duty 3: Participates as an expert on software, hardware, communications and new technology. Performs feasibility studies which involve evaluating proposals regarding modification or replacement of current software or hardware and development or acquisition of new technology. Analyzes information obtained by contact with senior management, functional analysts, users and through independent research. Explores design alternatives applying an understanding of network systems and data communications. Duty 4: As an IT expert, provides consultation and instruction. Advises functional area users on database and file accessing techniques, search strategies, processing and space utilization efficiencies, database security procedures, backup and program recovery techniques. Provides formal and informal training to ensure users understand the relationships of the system and are able to operate it without undue interruption. Prepares user manuals or instructions for assigned applications. Duty 5: Judiciously manages the acquisition, development and implementation of new technology. Manages all aspects of new or modified information systems, subsystems or equipment items to meet cost, schedule, performance and supportability criteria. Conducts mid- and long-range planning to ensure that program requirements receive consideration throughout the planning and programming cycle. Uses automated schedule and activity network development support tools, prepares Statements of Work (SOW) and performs technical contract management. Provides cost, schedule and performance management support to include development of program strategy, inputs SOW and other planning and programming documents. Reviews and evaluates contract proposals. Reviews contract deliverables and identifies potential problems, issues and concerns along with recommendations to the Configuration Management (CM) Manager. Assesses all pertinent issues found during the review and evaluation of contract proposals. Desired: 7+ years of dedicated experience in Information Assurance, Cybersecurity, or Systems Engineering within a DoD environment. PART-TIME OR UNPAID EXPERIENCE: Credit will be given for appropriate unpaid and or part-time work. You must clearly identify the duties and responsibilities in each position held and the total number of hours per week. VOLUNTEER WORK EXPERIENCE: Refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service Programs (i.e., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student and social). Volunteer work helps build critical competencies, knowledge and skills that can provide valuable training and experience that translates directly to paid employment. You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience.

The primary purpose of this position is to serve as the cybersecurity manager and principal advisor securing software systems, artificial intelligence technologies, and cloud environments to support military missions. In this role, you will direct cybersecurity operations and ensure systems meet strict federal and military standards.
Details.SubAgencyName: Air Force Life Cycle Management Center
Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: This job announcement may close at any time - apply now! The mission of the United States Air Force is: To fly, fight, and win ... Airpower anytime, anywhere. To achieve that mission, the Air Force has a vision of Global Vigilance, Global Reach and Global Power. That vision orbits around three core competencies: Developing Airmen, Technology-to-Warfighting and Integrating Operations. Core competencies and distinctive capabilities are based on a shared commitment to three core values -- integrity first, service before self, and excellence in all we do. Click here to view the AF Civilian Employment Eligibility Guide: US Citizen
MajorDuties: Serve as the principal advisor to the CISO, directing the overall cybersecurity program lifecycle, managing schedules, and translating complex technical risks into strategic mission objectives for senior leadership. Manage the Risk Management Framework (RMF) lifecycle and eMASS security authorization packages to ensure strict compliance with DoD, Air Force, and federal regulations across government cloud environments. Partner with software development teams to integrate automated vulnerability scanning and security controls into CI/CD pipelines, driving continuous Authorization to Operate (ATO) initiatives. Lead threat hunting operations and security incident investigations, while supervising the optimization of enterprise SIEM solutions to ensure rapid response and total network visibility. Design and enforce secure architectures for AI/ML workloads, mitigating adversarial artificial intelligence risks and ensuring secure Machine Learning Operations (MLOps) practices. Coordinate closely with technical support teams, ISSOs, and intelligence personnel to enforce DoD patch management protocols and system security configurations across both cloud and tactical environments.

MatchedObjectDescriptor.QualificationSummary: CYBER EXCEPTED SERVICE POSITIONS ARE NOT SUBJECT TO THE TWO-PAGE RESUME LIMIT. YOUR FULL RESUME WILL NEED TO BE UPLOADED TO YOUR USAJOBS PROFILE USING THE DOCUMENT TYPE "OTHER DOCUMENTS". This position is in the Professional work category at the Senior work level within the CES Occupational Structure. Who May Apply: Only applicants who meet one of the employment authority categories below are eligible to apply for this job. You will be asked to identify which category or categories you meet, and to provide documents which prove you meet the category or categories you selected. See Proof of Eligibility for an extensive list of document requirements for all employment authorities. Current Civilian Employees of the Organization Applying to Cyber Excepted Service (CES) Positions Army CES positions apply Veteran's Preference to preference eligible candidates, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., in accordance with the procedures provided in DoD Instruction 1400.25, Volume 3005, "CES Employment and Placement". If you are a veteran claiming veterans' preference, as defined by Section 2108 of Title 5 U.S.C., you must submit documents verifying your eligibility with your application package. In order to qualify, you must meet the experience requirements described below. Experience refers to paid and unpaid experience, including volunteer work done through National Service programs (e.g., Peace Corps, AmeriCorps) and other organizations (e.g., professional; philanthropic; religious; spiritual; community; student; social). You will receive credit for all qualifying experience, including volunteer experience. Your resume must clearly describe your relevant experience; if qualifying based on education, your transcripts will be required as part of your application. Additional information about transcripts is in this document. To qualify based on your experience, your resume must describe one year of specialized experience that demonstrates the possession of knowledge, skills, abilities, and competencies necessary for immediate success in the position. Such experience is typically in or directly related to the work of the position to be filled. Specialized experience would be demonstrated by Overseeing the planning and execution of security authorization reviews systems, enterprise networks, cloud operating environments, and other emerging technologies; Coaching/mentoring/training cybersecurity personnel to ensure execution of the Risk Management Framework; Developing and maintaining operational documentation and processes for risk management activities including plans of action and milestones for identified vulnerabilities; Reviewing security authorization documentation and technical artifacts to verify risk levels are within acceptable limits for assigned software and hardware. The specialized experience must include, or be supplemented by, information technology related experience (paid or unpaid experience and/or completion of specific, intensive training, as appropriate) which demonstrates each of the four competencies, as defined: (1) Attention to Detail - Is thorough when performing work and conscientious about attending to detail. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: completing thorough and accurate work independently, even in the most difficult or stressful situations; occasionally reviewing work completed by others. (2) Customer Service - Works with clients and customers (that is, any individuals who use or receive the services or products that your work unit produces, including the general public, individuals who work in the agency, other agencies, or organizations outside the Government) to assess their needs, provide information or assistance, resolve their problems, or satisfy their expectations; knows about available products and services; is committed to providing quality products and services. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: resolving routine and non-routine problems, questions, or complaints; developing and maintaining strong, mutually supportive working relationships with customers; conducting evaluation of support to determine quality of services and customer satisfaction, and recommending procedural changes based on customer need or changes in policy and/or regulation. (3) Oral Communication - Expresses information (for example, ideas or facts) to individuals or groups effectively, taking into account the audience and nature of the information (for example, technical, sensitive, controversial); makes clear and convincing oral presentations; listens to others, attends to nonverbal cues, and responds appropriately. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: convincingly conveying complex information to customers; presenting thoughts that are well-organized and demonstrating confidence in the facts and ideas; adjusting style when working with individuals with different levels of understanding; using various methods to explain and convey information. (4) Problem Solving - Identifies problems; determines accuracy and relevance of information; uses sound judgment to generate and evaluate alternatives, and to make recommendations. Examples of IT-related experience demonstrating this competency include: solving complex or sensitive problems by developing and proposing strategic alternatives; identifying possible conflicts and shared benefits; helping team anticipate problems and identifying and evaluating potential sources of information; providing feedback and coaching to others to help solve problems; engaging appropriate stakeholders when developing solutions in order to understand and incorporate multiple perspectives and needs; evaluating the effectiveness of decisions and adjusting future decisions as appropriate.

Details.AgencyMarketingStatement: Civilian employees serve a vital role in supporting the Army mission. They provide the skills that are not readily available in the military, but crucial to support military operations. The Army integrates the talents and skills of its military and civilian members to form a Total Army. The Army values diversity of perspectives, backgrounds, cultures and skills, which connects employees to organizations that are committed to building an inclusive work environment where they can contribute to their fullest potential. Are you interested in helping to defend our Nation? Exciting career opportunities are available with the U.S. Army Network Enterprise Technology Command (NETCOM)!
MajorDuties: Oversees the planning and execution of security authorization reviews and assurance case development for initial installation and ongoing operation of complex systems, enterprise networks and cloud operating environments.
Creates and delivers briefings, information papers, and other verbal and written communication for Army senior leaders at the General Officer and Senior Executive Service Member level.
Creates processes, measures of effectiveness, and measures of performance to, analyze, assess, maintain and provides information to Army Senior Leaders and other officials.
Synchronizes and manages the pre and post inspection actions, including monitoring progress through coordination with applicable cybersecurity staff.
Creates, publishes, and maintains technical procedures and processes within the command to document the cybersecurity posture of IT capabilities during an assessment and/or authorization
Creates, publishes, and maintains processes that ensures plans of actions and milestones are in place for vulnerabilities identified during risk assessments, audits, inspections, etc.
